News.title: ‘Devil’s Disciple’ serial killer, 73, refused parole again after serving more than 50 years in prison
News.content:
ONE of Britain’s longest serving prisoners, a serial killer dubbed the “Devil’s Disciple”, has been refused parole more than 50 years after a string of brutal killings that shocked the nation.

It comes three years after The Sun revealed how Patrick Mackay was being allowed back on the streets on day release.



Our photos showed him sauntering through Bristol city centre sporting a baseball cap and goatee beard, despite a history of sudden violence against frail pensioners and children.

The Parole Board has now rejected Mackay’s latest bid for release following a hearing earlier this year, concluding it was “not satisfied that release at this point would be safe for the protection of the public.”



The decision means the 73-year-old will remain behind bars after serving more than five decades in custody.

Mackay was jailed in 1975 after admitting responsibility for multiple killings carried out across west London and surrounding areas.

He targeted vulnerable victims, often gaining access to their homes before launching frenzied and violent assaults.

Among those he killed was 84-year-old widow Isabella Griffiths, who was beaten, strangled and stabbed in her Chelsea home.

Another victim, Adele Price, was murdered in similar circumstances after Mackay forced his way inside.

One of the most disturbing cases involved Father Anthony Crean, a Catholic priest who had previously tried to help him.



The priest was attacked with an axe in his own home, in a killing that ultimately led to Mackay’s arrest.

A summary of the parole decision reveals the panel described his original offences as “horrific and brutal”, adding that “the motivation and triggers that led to those offences are still, to a large extent, not understood”.

The hearing saw evidence from probation officers, prison officials and psychologists, as well as Mackay himself.



He had indicated through his legal team that he hoped to be released.

But the panel concluded that too many questions remain about his behaviour and risk.

It found that “no one would know how he might respond to the challenges he might face on release”, and warned that “his risk of reoffending [is] difficult to assess.”



Mackay has now served well beyond his original 20-year minimum term, which expired in 1995, and this was his 13th parole review.

News.title: Funny, fearless and outspoken Ann Widdecombe’s ‘murder’ raises many questions that deserve answers
News.content:
Justice for Ann

THE horrific murder of Ann Widdecombe sent shockwaves through Westminster — and across the country.

She was one of the best-known female politicians since the turn of the century.



Funny, fearless and outspoken, she devoted decades of her life to public service for the Conservative Party and, later, Reform UK.

But that was only part of her story. Millions with little interest in politics came to know her through Strictly, Big Brother and other TV appearances.



She was always herself: warm, witty and endlessly entertaining. Even those who disagreed with her politics often admitted she could raise a smile.

Tributes which poured in from across the political divide yesterday were a testimony to her legacy, led by Sir Keir Starmer. When a public figure is killed in such shocking circumstances, political differences are rightly put aside.

Many questions will be asked, which deserve answers. What was the motive for her killing, and are current and former MPs getting the protection they need?

Police must be as open as they can without jeopardising the investigation.

Above all else, there can only be one priority — the killer is brought to justice.

Shortcomings

ANDY Burnham’s path to power will be the swiftest since the office of Prime Minister was created in 1721.



Barely three weeks after being elected to Parliament, he is set to cross the threshold of Number 10 with the blanket endorsement of Labour MPs.

Minutes after nominations opened, they were scrambling over one other in a frantic dash to finish off their coup and complete the coronation of the self-styled King of the North.

But even before he gets through the famous black door, the problems are piling up for Burnham.

Eighty Labour MPs — a quarter of the 322 who nominated him to be leader — are demanding he scales back Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood’s sensible immigration crackdown.

If he refuses, he risks an early rebellion from the MPs who swept him into office. But caving in would alienate the millions of voters who hope he will address one of their greatest concerns.



Flinch over this, and his leadership could be over before it ever really began.

Miami spice

IT’S still a few hours before kick-off, but already Norway have had a cheap shot.

Not at the England team but at Prince William because he won’t be attending the World Cup clash in Miami tonight.

He is not a fair-weather fan, as they suggest, but has supported our national teams through thick and thin.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Let’s hope the spiteful dig will give the Three Lions exactly what they need . . .



The Will to win.

News.title: Family pay heartbreaking tribute to ‘bright light’ after woman, 42, dies in house fire
News.content:
BLAZE TRAGEDY Family pay heartbreaking tribute to ‘bright light’ after woman, 42, dies in house fire

A FAMILY have paid a heartbreaking tribute to their “bright light” after a woman died in a house fire.

Amy Louise Stafford, 42, died from severe burns in Southmead Hospital in Bristol on July 8.



Just hours earlier at around 5.25pm the emergency services had been called to a blaze at a property in Attlebridge Way in Kingsway, Gloucestershire.

Gloucestershire Police, along with crews from Gloucestershire Fire and Rescue Service and the South Western Ambulance Service, all attended the scene.



Cops and the fire services said the cause of the fire had not been established but they were “satisfied” there was no third-party involvement.

Amy’s family have now paid a touching tribute, saying: “A bright light in our lives has dimmed forever, our hearts will always seek out the warmth and love she brought to us all.”

They added: “Our beloved daughter and sister Amy has tragically been taken from us. We do not have adequate words to express how we feel.

“Our love goes out to all Amy’s family and friends near and far.

“Goodbye dearest Amy, sleep now, we are so proud of our independent lady.”

They also thanked the emergency services “who fought tirelessly” to try to save her.

News.title: Burnham backs Count Binface in by-election battle with Farage as Reform claim they’re being hit by ‘smear’ campaign
News.content:
ANDY Burnham turned to trash talk calling on voters to dispose of Nigel Farage in his Count Binface battle – as Reform loyalists said they were being hit by a “smear campaign”.

The Prime Minister-in-waiting got behind the underdog candidate after the main parties including Labour and the Tories refused to stand opponents in next month’s Clacton by-election.



Burnham was speaking at the O2 Silver Clef Awards for music on Thursday night as he heaped more pressure on Farage who is caught up in a slew of financial accusations.

He said: “I promise I’m not going to talk politics to you tonight except to say. Count Binface you are carrying the hopes of the nation, don’t let us down.”



Farage quit as an MP and decided to stand over scrutiny over his finances and a probe by Parliamentary authorities billing the vote as a “people versus the establishment”.

But the party’s deputy leader Richard Tice said Reform were being subjected to a smear campaign after it was was reported cops are investigating a £500,000 donation.

The cash concerns money given to them back in 2024 by Fiona Cottrell, The Times first said.

Tice told Times Radio: “This is all a politically motivated smear campaign.

“It’s outrageous. And I’m afraid, in a sense, it’s all this stuff which is why Nigel has said, ‘Enough is enough. I’m done with this. I’m going to take it to the good people of Clacton-on-the-Sea.’ This is not a coincidence.”

It comes after allegations that her convicted fraudster son George provided undeclared funding to Farage.



Meanwhile, Farage hit out at his opponents for not standing against him saing they have “acted in concert” as a uniparty.

He told Talk: “They’re trying to turn it into a joke. But, I mean, frankly, there shouldn’t just be a Clacton by-election going on. There should be a general election going on.

“We’ve got a new prime minister coming in, you know, who’s got no mandate of any kind at all. And I think the public are pretty sick of this game of musical chairs that goes on in Number 10.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe, 78, bludgeoned over head & body found in kitchen as ‘killer’ caught on CCTV at remote home
News.content:
A MAN of 26 is under arrest over the shocking murder of former minister and Strictly star Ann Widdecombe.

The 78-year-old was bludgeoned to death in her Dartmoor home — sustaining severe blunt trauma wounds to her head.



The body of Ms Widdecombe was found by a carer in remote Haytor, Devon.

It is believed the killer was caught on CCTV cameras at her home.



He was held at an address in Newton Abbot, Devon, 11 miles from the Dartmoor home, named Widdecombe’s Rest, which she shared with her cat.

Devon and Cornwall Police Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman said the death was not being treated as terrorism, and he had no information to suggest it was politically motivated.

Police were checking to see if Ms Widdecombe, a campaigner on stalking and harassment issues, had received any threats.

The former Conservative had become Reform UK’s immigration and justice spokeswoman.

ACC Longman refused to comment on if it could have been burglary gone wrong, adding: “We remain open-minded.”

A neighbour claimed a man driving a van had turned up in the middle of the night at Ms Widdecombe’s home.



What you need to know…

They said that the man was white and British, and dressed in hiking clothes.

Roads surrounding the home were sealed off for forensic examinations.



Announcing the arrest, ACC Longman said: “We can confirm that a 26-year-old man was arrested at an address in Newton Abbot. He remains in custody.”

Neighbours said Ms Widdecombe had withdrawn from the community after moving to the area in 2008.

Previously she had helped with events including setting up Widdecombe Fair. But recently she was seen only driving her silver Kia down the lanes or taking out her bins on Wednesdays.

Peter Cornthwaite, 66, from nearby Smokey Cross, said: “She changed the name of her house as soon as she moved in.

“We’ve seen her out and about. I’m quite shocked, it’s terrible.



“We never saw any security and she didn’t have a secure garden, no gate or anything.

“It’s very quiet round here. We leave our doors and windows unlocked. After renaming the house after herself, anyone who wanted to find her would have been able to.”

Retired Met Det Chief Insp Mick Neville appeared with Ms Widdecombe on GB News three weeks ago in a debate about prison sentencing.

He said: “She was still very much with it. Police have undoubtedly got their breakthrough with the suspect through CCTV, almost certainly from cameras at Ann’s home.

“While it remans unclear what the motive for her murder was, it is worth remembering that nine out of ten victims know their killers.



“Police will be looking to see whether there was anyone she may have met and possibly tried to help who might then have turned on her.

“They will also be checking to see whether there are any signs that her home was broken into.

“She’d been out of politics a long time and I think it’s unlikely that her political opinions could have enflamed someone to kill her at this stage. It’s shocking, almost beyond belief.



“After a lifetime of helping others and public service, it’s cruel and very unfair.”

The murder — first revealed by Sun Online yesterday — sent shock waves through the political world.

Sir Keir Starmer was briefed by Devon and Cornwall Chief Constable James Vaughan.

The PM said it was a moment to rise above any political differences and revealed he had spoken to Reform UK’s Nigel Farage, Labour’s Andy Burnham and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch.

Ms Widdecombe’s murder followed those of MPs Jo Cox and Sir David Amess in 2016 and 2021.



Speaking from Chequers, Sir Keir added: “It’s really important we remain vigilant.

“I’m not going to speculate about this particular case. This is really shocking news, and my thoughts will be with the family and friends of Ann Widdecombe at this awful time for them.

“Ann was a distinguished politician over many, many years with many achievements, and it’s a huge, huge loss.”

Mr Farage said: “She’s the best-known female politician since Margaret Thatcher. I don’t think anybody else comes close. And the fact that she was sporting enough to do, you know, Strictly Come Dancing, Big Brother.

“And then she was touring the country doing one-woman shows. She loved meeting people.”



Ms Badenoch said: “I’ve been stunned to hear this awful news. I don’t understand how someone could do something so horrific to an elderly person. My heart is breaking for her family.”

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the circumstances surrounding Ann Widdecome’s death were “extremely distressing”.

She added: “Ann’s dedication to public service was decades long, and she was a true servant of her constituents.”



Ms Widdecombe converted to Catholicism in the 1990s.

Her vicar nephew, Roger Widdecombe, of Cheltenham, Gloucs, was told of her death by cops, and said: “My thanks go to everybody who has sent messages of condolences.”

In 2010 she had TV viewers in stitches with her performances on Strictly, partnering Anton Du Beke. Fondly dubbed the worst dancer in the show’s history, she survived week after week thanks to the public vote.

Anton said: “I had the most brilliant time with Ann on Strictly. She became a real friend. She was fun, upbeat, positive, supportive.

“We had an incredible time together and stayed firm friends.



“My thoughts go out to all of her nearest and dearest and all her family.

“This is a sad day and I’m devastated by the news of Ann’s passing, but I shall remember her fondly, and miss her.”

Ms Widdecombe won more fans in 2018’s Celebrity Big Brother. She famously let her younger housemates give her a new look.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And she amused millions with her struggle to get her hair right with a pair of straighteners.

She continued to appear in the media discussing politics and made her last appearance on TalkTV on Wednesday.

News.title: ‘Go SOFT on migrants,’ Andy Burnham urged by Labour MPs as he faces immigration revolt before he’s even become PM
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is facing a Labour immigration revolt before he has even entered Downing Street.

Almost 80 of the party’s MPs have signed a private letter urging the Prime Minister-in-waiting to rethink Labour’s tougher migration agenda.



It comes just as Mr Burnham closes in on No10 after winning the backing of 322 Labour MPs — leaving him all but certain to become Britain’s next PM.

The left-wing backbenchers accused the Government of using “hostile rhetoric” on immigration, warning it has alienated progressive voters and left Labour talking “much more about control than compassion”.



They warned plans to make many legal migrants wait from ten to 20 years before qualifying for permanent settlement would make Britain “an international outlier”.

The letter said: “Targeting a group of migrants that followed the rules, and applying this retrospectively, does not pass the fairness test for a compassionate but firm system.



“We do not recall being asked on the doorstep to make it harder for migrant workers to settle in the UK.”

The MPs said Labour had been “blown off course” after trying to fight Reform UK “on Reform’s territory”.

The row comes as Mr Burnham weighs up whether to press ahead with the controversial settlement reforms.

He has backed the “broad thrust” of the policy but has previously questioned applying the tougher rules retrospectively to migrants already living in Britain.



The letter also piles fresh pressure on Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, one of Mr Burnham’s closest allies.

News.title: What ‘fed-up’ Clacton residents REALLY think of ‘crazy’ by-election as Nigel Farage and Count Binface go head to head
News.content:
UNDER the blazing sun and beady eyes of chip-stealing seagulls, the people of Clacton-on-Sea are preparing for the ­circus to come to town – a political circus, that is.

Reform UK leader Nigel ­Farage resigned as the Essex town’s MP on Tuesday amid sleaze allegations, triggering a by-election now due on August 13.



But if locals thought they were getting an ordinary contest, they were very much mistaken.

The Tories, Labour, Liberal Democrats and Greens have called Farage’s move a stunt and refused to contest the election.



Which leaves the space wide open for novelty candidate Count Binface, whose proposals include nationalising Adele and building “at least one affordable house”.

The “intergalactic space warrior” has received hundreds of donations this week, with Green energy tycoon Dale Vince even offering to fund his fight against Farage.



And Binface is not the only one challenging Farage for the seat, with at least eight other candidates saying they intend to stand.

Among them are Piers Corbyn, the brother of former Labour leader Jeremy, right-wing activist Laurence Fox, “Mr Fishfinger”, and wildlife campaigner Rob Pownall, who dresses as a fox.

Bookies currently have the Reform leader as odds-on to win, trailed by Count Binface at 4/1 according to William Hill.

When The Sun paid a visit to Clacton this week, most locals were fed up with the distractions and simply wished that things in their seaside town would improve.



Most are still backing their man in turquoise, who won a thumping 46 per cent of the vote at the 2024 General Election.

Others are willing to give him the benefit of the doubt over the current scandal — an undeclared gift of £5million — and still see him as the only person who can really take down the “establishment”.

“It’s crazy, it’s wasting time and money,” said retired autism support worker Debbie Eagle, 69.

“There’s such important issues facing the country — infrastructure, jobs . . . I feel sorry for the young people.”

Though still backing Farage for now, she added: “The country needs looking after, and a lot of the politicians are too busy fighting one another. Let’s just get on with it.



“They need to start shaping up.”

Elsewhere, some are ready to throw their lot in with the walking, talking bin, otherwise known as comedian Jon Harvey.

The silver-clad Count Binface has received support from all around the country, with more than 25,000 people donating to his campaign.



Harvey first made a name for himself in 2017, when he stood against Prime Minister Theresa May as Lord Buckethead.

Since then he has contested five more votes, including the past two

London Mayoral elections and the Makerfield by-election last month.

Among his new supporters is pensioner Phillip Chilton, 65, who told The Sun: “I’m fed up with everyone really. There hasn’t been much done for the community and all these elections aren’t going to do much for us. It’s just more chaos. I prefer the space alien. People are saying Count Binface is the next best thing to a genuine political contender, but he has to be one because no one else is really involved. I never thought in my life I would be voting for something like that, but that’s the state of British politics I guess.”

Primary school teacher Sandra Bullock, 64, told us: “I’m not a very political person, but another election is too much. It feels wrong really, but I have to admit I probably will vote for Count Binface. Put it this way, it can’t be any worse.”



Until calling the by-election, Farage was being investigated by Parliament’s ethics watchdog over his failure to declare a £5million gift from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne before the 2024 election.

He also faces questions about his relationship with George Cottrell, a businessman who was convicted of fraud in the US in 2017.

Farage denies all wrongdoing, and this week held a press conference to declare that his future should be decided by the people of Clacton.

“This will be a people versus the establishment by-election,” he added.

Other parties responded by branding it a stunt.



Writing on X, Chancellor Rachel Reeves said: “It is a farce and a desperate distraction, and the people of Clacton deserve better.

“But if he wants to spend the summer arguing with a bin, I won’t stop him.”

After his expected re-election, however, Farage will still be under investigation.



And if the findings go against him, he will have to step down. It means locals already tired of the polling booth could be set for yet another visit in just a few months.

But to plenty of people out enjoying the warm weather in the town, all that matters is that Farage is the only politician saying what they want to hear.

Pensioner Margaret Day, 81, is one of them.

She told The Sun of the recent criticism: “It’s all a load of rubbish. He’s done a lot of work helping people in the constituency, helping people who were in trouble.”

Once a Labour voter before moving to the Conservatives, the former school kitchen worker is now “all for Nigel”. She added: “I’m definitely voting for him. I’d support him either way.”



On his way down to the beachfront, semi-retired Mark Monte, 59, said that Farage could count on his support and believes that he is being hounded by the media.

Talking about the MP’s decision to resign, he said: “We all know that he’s done it so he can go out and then come back, but I do support his politics. I think some people will be turned off by it, but I’m hoping he will still get in.

“I want to see him as the Prime Minister, I want radical change.

“But if there’s a by-election after this, I don’t think people will be happy. There’s only so many times before people just won’t come out to vote.”

Restaurant owner Jason Smedley, 55, is also a supporter. He rents out part of his building to Reform, who use it as their local HQ.



He told The Sun: “You get told, ‘Oh he’s done this with the money, this and that’. I don’t care. He’s a very successful businessman.

“I don’t think people care. He’s adamant, and innocent until proven guilty. I’ll take him at face value.”

Selling ice cream in a hut is Maddison Dunsdon, 20, who agrees with Farage but isn’t convinced she’ll vote for him. “I’ll probably go with Count Binface, because that’s my sense of humour.”

Self-described lady of leisure Catherine Taddei, 81, is also a big fan of Farage’s. But his latest move left her confused and thinking he had resigned to ditch the town.

“I thought he’d done a dirty trick, but I’m glad he’s standing again,” she said.



Also in the town centre is a rare breed — a Labour voter in the form of retiree Barry Cannack, 75.

“If he had nothing to hide, why did he resign?” he said.

Few get a better sense of the circus than Station Bar landlady Karen Baily, 60, who is used to seeing the backs of the Westminster elite as they rush off to catch the train to London after campaigning.



For her, Farage’s resignation is just a sign that he knows the game is up.

She says: “He isn’t for the town. He’s just for himself. He’s not here as often as he should be, and he only goes around when the Press is about. I think resigning is just a cover-up.

“He should have got the truth out there at the beginning and it would be out there.

“People here are still going to vote for him, because of the small boats and things like that — you had boats landing on the beach here last weekend. But the town is going downhill.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There is at least one person, however, who is certainly not letting politics get in the way of life. Ice cream hut server Anita Buckman, 54, tells us with a smile: “Nigel Fr-aage? How do you say his name again?



“I’ve seen him on telly a lot lately, but I don’t take much interest. It will be what it will be.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe 'murder' police provide motive update with death not treated as terror or politically-motivated
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe 'murder' police provide motive update with death not treated as terror or politically-motivated

Devon and Cornwall Police have launched a murder investigation into the death of 78-year-old politician Ann Widdecombe, and have arrested a '26-year-old white British man'

View 3 Images Detectives arrested a white British man on Friday afternoon, in the nearby town of Newton Abbot (Image: Matt Keeble/PA Wire)

Police who arrested a man on suspicion of the murder of former MP Ann Widdecombe do not think her death is politically motivated.

The 78-year-old was found dead at her bungalow in Haytor, a village on Dartmoor, Devon on Thursday morning. The former Conservative MP, who later became a Brexit Party MEP and subsequently a Reform UK spokesperson, lived in the property alone. She was reportedly discovered by a carer covered in blood after sustaining at least one serious head wound.

Police have not confirmed the cause of death, which was announced this morning. A 26-year-old white British man has been arrested on suspicion of her murder and remains in police custody. He was detained in Newton Abbot, a town around 10 miles from the home of the tragic former Stricitly Come Dancing star.

View 3 Images Ann Widdecombe has died aged 78 (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Devon and Cornwall Police's Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman told a press conference earlier that there was "no information that this is a politically-motivated crime" and also confirmed the incident was not being treated as terror-related.

It has not been disclosed if anything was stolen during the attack, or if the killer had broken into the house or if they used a weapon.

Detective Chief Inspector Ilona Rosson said the investigation was moving quickly. DCI Rosson said: "This is an extremely tragic incident and our thoughts are very much with the family and friends of Ann Widdecombe at this difficult time.

"Our murder inquiry is in its early stages but moving at a significant pace. We are deploying all of the necessary resources to find out exactly what has happened and to locate the person responsible who we believe to be a white male."

Just over two hours later, the force confirmed they had arrested a suspect. Chief Constable Longman said the inquiry was “in its early stages” but “moving at significant pace”.

View 3 Images Police outside her home in Haytor, Dartmoor (Image: Matt Keeble/PA Wire)

He added: “We are deploying all the necessary resources to find out exactly what has happened. I would appeal to anyone who may have information about this incident, however insignificant it may seem, to come forward and speak with us.”

Police were called to the house in Haytor Vale, a village within the Dartmoor National Park, at about 11.40am on Thursday by the ambulance service. Ms Widdecombe, who lived alone, was pronounced dead at the scene. Her next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.

The former MP retired in 2001 and moved into her Devon home, which she called Widdecombe's Rest, in 2008. Asked in 2013 if she was ever afraid of being attacked because she could easily be found, she said: "I am never scared, or lonely. I'm content."

She said in the interview: “I've never gone in for the big gates and the electronics and all that nonsense. So, no, I mean, anybody could come in and steal a gnome. I would pick them up on my cameras so if anybody wants to steal a gnome they'd better mask up.”

She also said she did get death threats but would ignore them. She said: “I used to get death threats from time to time. We all did, and my staff would say, 'shall we tell the police?' And I'd say, 'put it in the bin, because if the IRA are going to do it, they're not going to tell you in advance, they're just going to do it.'

Article continues below

"And I still take that attitude. I do know that we're in a slightly different world. I do know that. But I think it's crucial that MPs and their constituents intermingle freely.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe murder probe: 'Mystery hiker' seen at ex-Tory MP's home in dead of night as man, 26, arrested
News.content:
Devon and Cornwall Police launched a murder probe after ex-Conservative MP and Brexit Party MEP Ann Widdecombe was found dead inside her home with "serious injuries", with a man arrested on suspicion of murder

Ann Widdecombe murder probe: 'Mystery hiker' seen at ex-Tory MP's home in dead of night as man, 26, arrested

Police have arrested a 26-year-old white, British man on suspicion of murder, after Ann Widdecombe was found dead inside her Devon home, aged 78.

Police said it remained "open-minded" about the investigation, and said it had no information to believe her death was politically-motivated.

Ms Widdecombe's agent, confirming the death, said: "It is with great sadness that today we announce the death of the Rt Hon Ann Widdecombe, DSG. We send our deepest condolences to Ann's family and friends. We ask that the family's wish not to be contacted at this sad time is respected."

The long-time Tory switched allegiance to the Brexit Party in 2019, and then to Reform UK. She had lived alone in Haytor since retiring as the MP for Maidstone and The Weald in 2010.

News.title: Stratford station evacuated live: 'Avoid area' warning as huge fire breaks out near tracks
News.content:
London Fire Brigade full statement as crews to remain on scene 'for much of the evening'

Eight fire engines and around 60 firefighters remain at the scene of the fire at Stratford train station.

As of 8.45pm, multiple seats of fire involving trees, shrubbery and grass near the railway tracks were still alight.

People have been told to avoid the area while fire crews work to tackle the blaze.

Station Commander Scott Thorpe, who is at the scene, said:"This fire is predominantly located within an area of grass and shrubbery that is surrounded on all sides by railway tracks.

"Crews are also working to extinguish other pockets of fire in around the station's sidings.

"The power to the railway tracks has been isolated and the Brigade is working closely with its partners in order to resolve this incident safely.

"Firefighters are making steady progress; however we expect crews to remain on scene for much of the evening."

Stratford station, which has been evacuated, remains closed and all passengers were evacuated.

London Fire Brigade said firefighters are currently assisting British Transport Police to safely get passengers off a number of trains that had to stop near the station.

As a result of the fire, Transport for London (TfL) services are also disrupted.

Around 40 calls were made to LFB about the fire, with the first coming in just before 7pm.

Crews from Plaistow, Poplar, Ilford, Bethnal Green and surrounding fire stations have been sent to the scene.

News.title: Spain wildfires live: 12 dead in Almeria 'including Brits' near expat village
News.content:
Twelve people have been killed in a wildfire in Los Gallardos, Almería, Spain - at least four of the dead are thought to be British and were found in a burnt out car

FOUR Brits 'feared DEAD in Spain' after burnt out car found in WILDFIRE in Los Gallardos

Several Brits are feared to have died in a wildfire in Spain which has claimed 12 lives. Local reports suggest three of the dead are children.

Officials said four people found dead in a burned out car in Los Gallardos, Almería are believed to be British. There are also fears that Brits could be among a group of people found dead while trying to escape the flames on foot.

Witnesses say the wildfire was caused by a downed power line. Around 150 firefighters have been deployed to tackle the fire in a village called Bedar, alongside military personnel.

A source said the village is made up of roughly 70 per cent British inhabitants, most of whom are elderly and retired there.

News.title: BRENDAN COX: 'Senseless death of Ann Widdecombe brings back pain of my precious wife Jo Cox's murder'
News.content:
BRENDAN COX: 'Senseless death of Ann Widdecombe brings back pain of my precious wife Jo Cox's murder'

Ten years ago, Labour MP Jo Cox was shot and stabbed to death by a far-right extremist and her ex husband Brendan Cox hopes Ann Widdecombe's death provokes a similar coming-together

View 3 Images Jo and Brendan Cox on their wedding day, years before her life was snatched away (Image: Raworth and Raworth Photography)

I never knew Ann Widdecombe, but you could tell from afar that she had a mischievous sense of fun and believed things with a passion.

‌



She wasn’t someone who changed her views or adapted them for convenience, or to keep up with the times – and, while I disagreed with her on so many things, her passion and sincerity was obvious.

‌



So it came as a horrific shock to hear of the news of her death. I think we probably all assumed that Ann’s death was from natural causes.

‌



It wouldn’t have occurred to anyone that someone in her twilight years would have been subjected to what sounds like a horrific and senseless attack.

View 3 Images A man has tonight been arrested on suspicion of murder after Ann Widdecombe was found dead (Image: Getty Images)

‌



How political firebrand Ann Widdecombe traded life in London for the 'bleakness' of Dartmoor READ MORE :

Ann Widdecombe's final TV and public appearances before her death aged 78 READ MORE :

We obviously don’t know and can’t speculate on the motivation, rationale and motive for the attack. But what we can say is that there is nothing that could ever justify an attack like this.

Of course for me it brings back all of the pain and emotion of losing Jo when she was murdered and I have a real sense of what Ann’s family will be going through - the shock followed by the numbness followed by the rawness followed by the pain.

View 3 Images Brendan Cox says the politician's death brings the memories rushing back (Image: Adam Gerrard/Daily Mirror)

Article continues below

I hope the whole country comes together as they did when Jo was killed, to honour somebody who was a real public servant and who believed in doing her best to represent the people that she cared about.

Moments like this should pull us together as a country in shock, in solidarity, and in sympathy with everybody who is in pain from this horrific, senseless and outrageous murder.

News.title: Prince Harry live: Duke, Meghan and kids ALL visit Charles while Kate steps out with William
News.content:
Prince Harry is spending the day at a one-year to go celebration for his Invictus Games in Birmingham today - but he will not be joined by wife Meghan Markle as originally planned

Prince Harry live: Duke, Meghan and kids ALL visit Charles while Kate steps out with William

The King has been reunited with his grandchildren after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited the head of state at his country home, it is understood.

Charles welcomed Meghan and Harry’s children to his Highgrove residence during the afternoon after days of speculation over whether the family meeting would take place.

Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, last saw their grandfather in person during Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations in 2022.

It is understood the Queen who has a private home near to the King’s Gloucestershire property was also among the group.

The meeting between Charles and the young prince and princess is likely to be interpreted as a sign of the thawing of the relationship between the King and his son Harry.

His rift with William is ongoing and shows no sign of abating and the family reunion took place during the same afternoon William was playing in a charity polo match at Windsor.

The Princess of Wales made a surprise appearance too to cheer on her husband as he took part in the DMMI Royal Charity Polo Cup 2026 at Guards Polo Club.

In February 2024 Harry made a transatlantic dash from his Californian home to Britain to see his father following his cancer diagnosis, which may have led to the first steps in a reconciliation between the pair.

Harry had planned to bring his family to the UK while he undertook a week-long series of events promoting charities and organisations close to his heart including the Invictus Games he founded.

Security issues prevented Meghan and the children travelling with him on Monday but it appears concerns over safety were mitigated to allow the visit to Highgrove to take place.

The Mirror exclusively reported this week the monarch, 77, instructed senior aides to engage in ongoing talks with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, to secure time in his busy diary around his public duties.

Within hours of Prince Harry's solo Invictus Games event drawing to a close in Birmingham, Princess Kate stepped out to support her husband Prince William.

For updates on Prince Harry and the Royal Family, follow our live blog below...

News.title: Ann Widdecombe 'covered in blood and discovered by carer' as police arrest man on suspicion of murder
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe 'covered in blood and discovered by carer' as police arrest man on suspicion of murder

Asked in 2013 if she was ever afraid of being attacked because she could easily be found, ex-Tory MP Ann Widdecombe said: "I am never scared, or lonely. I'm content."

View 12 Images Ann Widdecombe was found dead in her Devon home

A 26-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of the murder of former Conservative MP Ann Widdecombe.

The 78-year-old former minister and TV star was found with "serious injuries" in her bungalow on the edge of Dartmoor, Devon on Thursday morning. She was reportedly discovered by a carer covered in blood after sustaining at least one serious head wound. Police have not confirmed the cause of death.

Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman said there was no evidence to suggest the murder was politically motivated, adding that it was "too early" to say whether the suspect was known to her. The man, a white British national, was detained on Friday afternoon in Newton Abbott, around eight miles from the murder scene. Detectives are not treating the incident as terror related.

It is not clear if anything was stolen during the attack, if the killer had broken into the house or if they used a weapon. At 3.50 on Friday afternoon, Devon and Cornwall Police announced that the force had launched a murder inquiry.

View 12 Images Ann Widdecombe died aged 78 (Image: UK Parliament)

Detective Chief Inspector Ilona Rosson said the investigation was “moving at a significant pace".

“This is an extremely tragic incident and our thoughts are very much with the family and friends of Ann Widdecombe at this difficult time,” DCI Rosson said.

"Our murder inquiry is in its early stages but moving at a significant pace. We are deploying all of the necessary resources to find out exactly what has happened and to locate the person responsible who we believe to be a white male."

Just over two hours later the force confirmed they had arrested a suspect. Mr Longman said the inquiry was “in its early stages” but “moving at significant pace”.

View 12 Images She was found dead at her home (Image: Matt Keeble/PA Wire)

He added: “We are deploying all the necessary resources to find out exactly what has happened. I would appeal to anyone who may have information about this incident, however insignificant it may seem, to come forward and speak with us.”

Police were called to the house in Haytor Vale, a village within the Dartmoor National Park, at about 11.40am on Thursday by the ambulance service. Ms Widdecombe, who lived alone, was pronounced dead at the scene. Her next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.

She last appeared in public on Wednesday morning on Talk TV to back Nigel Farage in the Clacton by-election. Detectives from the Major Crime Investigation Team are conducting "extensive enquiries" as they build a timeline of her movements from that moment to the time of her death.

They will also be looking at the extensive CCTV in and around her home as they attempt to trace the movements of her killer before and after the murder. Officers will be examining ANPR cameras to follow the movements of any vehicle that might have been used in the attack.

View 12 Images Matt Longman delivered today's press conference for Devon and Cornwall Police (Image: BBC)

The former MP retired in 2001 and moved into her Devon home, which she called Widdecombe's Rest, in 2008. Asked in 2013 if she was ever afraid of being attacked because she could easily be found, she said: "I am never scared, or lonely. I'm content."

In October during a light hearted interview, she was asked about the gnomes in her garden and security.

Police statement as murder inquiry launched into death of Ann Widdecombe

She said “I've never gone in for the big gates and the electronics and all that nonsense. So, no, I mean, anybody could come in and steal a gnome. I would pick them up on my cameras so if anybody wants to steal a gnome they'd better mask up.”

She also said she did get death threats but would ignore them. She said: “I used to get death threats from time to time. We all did, and my staff would say, 'shall we tell the police?' And I'd say, 'put it in the bin, because if the IRA are going to do it, they're not going to tell you in advance, they're just going to do it.' And I still take that attitude. I do know that we're in a slightly different world. I do know that. But I think it's crucial that MPs and their constituents intermingle freely.”

View 12 Images Ann Widdecombe said she'd often get death threats, but ignored them (Image: Steve Taylor/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

‌



Ms Widdecombe told how she was a good friend of former Tory Southend West MP David Amess who was stabbed to death in a terror attack in 2021.

She said: “I knew him terribly well, and his family, of course. And I know, and I said this to his widow, who agreed with me, that he would never want his death used as a reason to distance MPs from their constituents. His belief, and it is still my belief, that an MP should be able to walk through the town on a Saturday afternoon, talk to their constituents. Absolutely. So I feel very strongly about that."

David's daughter, Katie, said: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Ann Widdecombe. Ann was a loyal and longstanding friend to my father, Sir David Amess, and our family will always be grateful for the kindness, strength and dignity she showed in the most difficult moments of our lives.

‌



View 12 Images Scene at 'Widdecombe's Rest' as police investigate her death (Image: Alamy Live News.)

"Her eulogy for my father at Westminster Cathedral, and the compassion she offered us in the days and months that followed his death, reflected the very best of her character — warm, principled, and unwavering in her support for those she cared about.

"Ann’s friendship meant a great deal to my father, and her words brought comfort to so many who loved him. Today, we remember her with affection and respect, and we send our heartfelt condolences to her family and friends. May she rest in peace.”

‌



A cordon remained in place last night around the murder scene while specialist officers continued forensic examinations. Several police cars were lined up on the road outside of her rural house, while a van was parked on her driveway. A forensics vehicle was also at the scene. Her home is surrounded by large green spaces, with few houses nearby.

View 12 Images Forensic teams were investigating the scene all day (Image: Matt Keeble/PA Wire)

One officer was guarding the crime scene. A cat bowl with food still in it could be seen at the front of the property - believed to be for her pet, Aloysius, who survives her.

‌



Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer responded to the murder probe announcement by saying it was important to “rise above any political differences”. Speaking at Chequers before the arrest, he said he would not speculate on any potential motive but urged the public to help catch the “clearly dangerous” suspect.

The Prime Minister said he had spoken to his expected successor Andy Burnham, Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK’s Nigel Farage about the case. The ex-Tory prisons minister later became a Brexit Party MEP and subsequently a Reform UK spokeswoman. She also found fame outside politics after starring in Strictly Come Dancing.

View 12 Images A man has been arrested on suspicion of Ann Widdecombe's murder (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Kemi Badenoch said she was "stunned" to hear the news. The Conservative leader said: "I've really struggled to find the words to say. Ann Widdecombe was a very fun and feisty woman who spoke her mind. She was 78-years-old, she was an elderly woman. I don't understand how someone can do something so horrific to an elderly person. It is a nasty, horrific attack. My heart is breaking for her family. It's one thing when someone dies but to know that they have been murdered in this horrible way is just awful."

She said the Conservative Party was "reeling" at the loss and sent condolences to Nigel Farage and Reform, the party Ms Widdecombe had joined after a decades-long career as a Conservative MP and minister.

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said: "I’m really shocked and distressed at the news about Ann Widdecombe. She was a woman of deep faith who devoted her life to public service.

‌



"The idea that she could have been murdered is truly horrifying. My thoughts and prayers are with her family and all who loved her."

12 View 12 Images Ann Widdecombe was previously a Conservative minister, and a Brexit Party MEP (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock) 12 View 12 Images She finished second in the 2018 edition of Celebrity Big Brother (Image: Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images)

‌



In a post on X, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the death of Ann Widdecombe. The circumstances of her death are extremely distressing and my thoughts are with Ann’s family and loved ones. Ann’s dedication to public service was decades long, and she was a true servant of her constituents.

“I have spoken to the Chief Constable of Devon and Cornwall police today. The Home Office stands ready to provide whatever support they need with their ongoing investigation. I urge everyone to avoid speculation and allow the police investigation to progress.”

View 12 Images The former government minister and long-time MP was found dead after suffering "serious injuries" at her home (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

‌



Miss Widdecombe’s management firm Cloud 9 urged people with information to contact the police and said: “We are absolutely devastated by this news following a very traumatic and upsetting 24 hours.”

Strictly Come Dancing’s Anton Du Beke said he was “devastated” to hear that Ann Widdecombe has died. The pair were partnered together on the BBC One dancing programme in 2010.

In a video shared on X prior to police announcing they had launched a murder investigation into her death, he said: “I had the most brilliant time with Ann on Strictly Come Dancing."

‌



View 12 Images Anyone with information was urged to contact the police after Ann's death (Image: Sky News)

Meanwhile, Brendan Cox - husband of murdered MP Jo Cox - said Ann's death brought memories back of Jo's senseless murder in 2016.

He told the Mirror: "I never knew Ann Widdecombe, but you could tell from afar that she had a mischievous sense of fun and believed things with a passion. She wasn’t someone who changed her views or adapted them for convenience, or to keep up with the times – and, while I disagreed with her on so many things, her passion and sincerity was obvious.

Article continues below

“So it came as a horrific shock to hear of the news of her death. I think we probably all assumed that Ann’s death was from natural causes. It wouldn’t have occurred to anyone that someone in her twilight years would have been subjected to what sounds like a horrific and senseless attack.

“Of course for me it brings back all of the pain and emotion of losing Jo when she was murdered and I have a real sense of what Ann’s family will be going through - the shock followed by the numbness followed by the rawness followed by the pain. I hope the whole country comes together as they did when Jo was killed, to honour somebody who was a real public servant and who believed in doing her best to represent the people that she cared about.

“Moments like this should pull us together as a country in shock, in solidarity, and in sympathy with everybody who is in pain from this horrific, senseless and outrageous murder.”

News.title: Donald Trump is quietly doing everything you'd do if you wanted to undermine an election
News.content:
Donald Trump is quietly doing everything you'd do if you wanted to undermine an election

The systematic way in which Trump is targeting and neutering the little-known, bipartisan barriers to meddling is getting harder to ignore - here's everything you need to know about that and more from Trumpworld

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump is quietly doing exactly what you'd do if you wanted to overturn the result of an election you didn't like.

‌



Undermining faith in American elections among the general public isn't new for Trump. It's one of his favourite pastimes. But the systematic way in which Trump is targeting and neutering the little-known, bipartisan barriers to meddling is getting harder to ignore. And with the Midterm elections just months away, it's increasingly looking like he isn't in a mood to wait for the result.

‌



Let's take a minute to look at the two new ways he's trying to undermine and control the way Americans vote before we get into the regular roundup.

‌



He gutted a crucial elections watchdog

Two weeks ago, the Supreme Court ruled that Trump had the power to shape the membership and leadership of government bodies that were designed to be independent. And yesterday he used those powers to effectively dismantle the Election Assistance Commission - firing the two Democratic members of the four-person board and accepting the resignation of a Republican member. The other Republican quit earlier in the year.

The Commission is responsible for maintaining voter registration forms and certifying voting machines and equipment. It was formed after the farce of the 2000 election, where the result took weeks to be finalised because of recounts and court challenges in Florida.

The White House said Trump "reserves the right to remove individuals that may not be totally aligned with the important task of securing America's elections and ensuring every legal vote is counted."

‌



He's still trying to force Congress to pass his election meddling bill

Regular readers will be familiar with the SAVE America Act, Trump's bid to make sweeping changes to the way Americans can vote. It would demand strict photo ID to register to vote, seize control of voter rolls on an unprecedented scale, and dramatically clamp down on postal voting - which Trump has repeatedly and falsely claimed is vulnerable to fraud.

It will never pass through Congress. Trump hasn't got the votes and Congress won't give up the filibuster to force it through.

View 2 Images Trump has been trying to strongarm congress (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The whatabuster?

A filibuster is where one party can block another party's bill getting to a vote by literally standing up and talking without stopping. It's a bad look for the party trying to push the law through, because it calls attention to it. And you need 60 votes in the Senate to break a filibuster, and the Republicans only have 51. They can change the rules with a simple majority to ban the filibuster, but that would risk Democrats tearing up loads of laws that they like with no way of stopping them next time they get in. It's like mutually assured destruction but for Congress.

Still, Trump continues to strong-arm Republicans into ramming it through

His latest method of extortion against his own party has been his refusal to sign the Housing bill. Long story short, the current housing bill has broad bipartisan support and is generally considered to be A Good Thing.

Trump could not be less interested in it, regardless of whether it makes it easier for regular Americans to buy or build homes. He's referred to it as a "yawn".

‌



But in it, Trump thought he saw an opportunity, so he held it to ransom. He refused to sign it at the very last minute, denying Congress what could be its last bill signing before the election.

Thing is though, he can only sit on it for 10 days, at which point it becomes law whether he signs it or not. Unless he vetoes it, which he probably ...maybe..won't do.

He posted on Truth Social today saying it was a point of protest - and effectively threatened consequences for those who didn't let him get his way.

‌



"I will not sign the Housing Bill, which has been fully approved by Congress and sent to the White House, in PROTEST over the fact that the United States Senate is not capable of passing THE SAVE AMERICA ACT," Trump wrote.

"THE SAVE AMERICA ACT'S non-passage is CRAZY, and a serious threat to any politician who votes against it!

Trump has threatened to bomb Iran from beyond the grave

Donald Trump has told the New York Post that he's left instructions "if anything happens, to just literally bomb them at levels that they've never seen before." He added: "I've been No. 1 [on Iran's kill list] for a long time, and it's the way life is, you know. I hope you'll miss me"

‌



There is, of course, no legal basis for this. If Trump dies it would be up to his successor to decide whether to honour his wishes.

Kristi Noem is getting a divorce

Shortly after she was sacked as Homeland Security Secretary by Trump, you may remember Kristi Noem was "blindsided" by a real marmalade dropper of a story about her husband, Byron. Mr Noem, it emerged, had been participating in online fetish forums, posting photos of himself wearing pink hot pants and enormous fake breasts. The revelation came after a huge amount of speculation about the nature of Mrs Noem's relationship with close aide Corey Lewandowski. Asked at a Congressional committee if they were in a sexual relationship, Ms Noem branded the allegation "tabloid garbage" and a "disgusting lie."

It came as a surprise to nobody today when it was revealed that Kristi and Byron Noem are to divorce.

‌



Trump is making it even harder for people to see the White House

There are currently two ways to see the White House in person - from Lafayette Park to the north, and from the Ellipse to the south. In normal times, it's actually quite impressive how close you can get to the "People's House" - though the huge iron fences serve as a reminder that it's one of the most secure premises on the planet.

I say in normal times, because increasingly one or both of the Ellipse and Lafayette Park is fenced off these days. This is an annoyance for a number of reasons. As well as being a hotspot for tourists, Lafayette Park is the traditional place where people come to protest.

I think I've only been down to Lafayette Park once since Trump returned to office and found it open. It's sometimes closed for security reasons - but since Trump came back it's mostly been because he's been redecorating. He's given the fountains in the park a once-over - and added a really gross RGB lighting package. And he's repaved the paths, which were perfectly fine as they were. There's some suspicion the renovations were planned to prevent people getting close enough to the bulldozed East Wing to see the ongoing work.

‌



Anyway, on the other side of the building, the Ellipse is often closed for events, or simply for days when Marine One is landing on the South Lawn. Which is a lot. And when both of these parks are closed you really can't get a good look at the People's House from either angle.

Well, tonight the Trump Administration submitted a proposal to put Lafayette Park behind a permanent fence. The plan indicates that it would still allow public access. But it would mean the Secret Service would no longer have to erect temporary fencing every time they close the park - meaning the barrier to closure would be much lower. For journalists, for activists and for touritsts, this would be a terrible move.
